headline: Approved design-build plan for a new 5,024-square-foot animal control facility on Vincent P. Kelly Road.
summary: The committee reviewed a cost analysis for a new animal control facility of about 5,000 square feet. Members discussed renovating 30 Cross Street, which is 10,000 square feet, but the city said it could not secure regional partners and did not need that much space. The committee voted unanimously to proceed with design and construction through a design-build firm selected by a request for proposals.
decisions: Approved proceeding with design and construction of a new animal control facility on Vincent P. Kelly Road using a design-build method. Vote was unanimous.

decision_titles: Animal control facility on Vincent P. Kelly Road
plain_text:
City of Bristol 
ANIMAL CONTROL BUILDING COMMITTEE 
SPECIAL MEETING  
August 18th, 2026 
111 North Main Street 
Bristol, CT 06010 
 
 
PRESENT:     ABSENT:    
Lindsey Rivers, Public Works Analyst Luis Lorenzo, Maintenance Technician   
Frank Stawski, Commissioner    
Lynn DellaBianca, Commissioner 
Jon Mace, Commissioner 
Nancy Levesque, Commissioner  
Christopher Hayden, Commissioner  
Holly Goodwin, Commissioner  
 
STAFF PRESENT: 
Ellen Zoppo-Sassu, Mayor of Bristol  
Lukasz Burkacki, Civil Engineer  
 Raymond Rogozinski, Director of Public Works  
 
 
1. CALL TO ORDER 
Commissioner Christopher Hayden called the meeting to order at 5:00 pm.  
 
2. PUBLIC PARTICIPATION 
NONE 
 
3. ANIMAL CONTROL FACILITY – SUMMARY & PRESENTATION OF 
COST ESTIMATE 
a. Memo Cost Est. Presentation  
Civil Engineer Lukas Burkacki reviewed the cost analysis completed by KEHES Group. 
The purposed animal control facility is will be approximately 5,000 square feet and 
estimated to cost 4,133,116 million dollars.  
 
b. Animal Control Facility Assessment  
This document breaks down the square footage of the purposed size of the animal control 
facility.  
 
Director of Public Works Raymond Rogozinski spoke to the committee how this 
purposed building on Vincent P Kelley is based on the scope of the project and what we 
need for an Animal Control Facility. Commissioner Frank Stawski and Jon Mace spoke 
one how it would be helpful to see the comparison between renovating 30 Cross Street 
and building on Vincent P Kelley Rd.
Major Ellen Zoppo-Sassu told the committee that the City of Bristol is unable to secure 
regional partners. 30 Cross Street is 10,000 square feet compared to the purposed 5,000 
square foot building. The need for 10,000 square feet is not necessary for our current 
volume of animals being brought in. The mayor also mentioned how a design build 
system would save time and cost on this project.  
 
4. COST ESTIMATE AND RECOMMENDATION TO PROCESS/ PREPARE & 
ISSUSE AN RFP TO PROCURE A DESIGN & BUILD FIRM  
 
a. Animal Control Facility – Layout Plan 
b. Building Assessment Animal Control Facility 
c. Action to Proceed – Memo From Raymond Rogozinski 
 
Director of Public Works Raymond Rogozinski clarified with the committee that they 
will decide on the direction the project will go. The public work recommendation is to 
proceed with a design build. The committee discussed the pros and cons of going with a 
design build. Raymond Rogozinski further explained how design build would work and 
would still give the committee control over the project and design of the building. The 
2029 state regulations will be met with using a design build. Further discussion was had 
on the design build option.  
 
Commissioner Jon Mace made the motion to approve proceeding with design and 
construction of a new Animal Control facility on Vincent P. Kelly Road. The proposed 
facility shall consist of a building with new an area of approximately 5,024 square feet 
and include 30 primary animal enclosures, 30 exercise runs, animal isolation areas, a 
garage, a cat kennel room, an exotic animal room, and supporting operational spaces 
identified in the DPW Engineering facility assessment. With the caveat of meeting all 
animal control building regulations.  
 
Said approval shall authorize of a design-build delivery method. DPW will use prepare a 
Request for Proposals and coordinate with the City Purchasing Department to procure a 
single qualified firm responsible for architectural & engineering services along with 
construction of a new building. The project new scope shall include City land-use 
approval (Zoning Commission or Planning Commission). The project shall also include 
the mechanical and ventilation systems necessary for animal housing and operations, 
including air conditioning. Seconded by Lindsey Rivers. 
 
Further discussion was had regarding the RFP process.  
  Vote: Unanimously Passed  
 
 
5. ADJOURNMENT  
Commissioner Frank Stawski made a motion to adjourn, seconded by Commissioner Jon 
Mace.  
   Vote: Unanimously Passed
The Animal Control Building Committee regular meeting on August 18th 2026 was 
hereby adjourned at 5:42pm. 
 
Jacqueline England   
Recording Secretary
